name: Benjamin Yang
bio: Benjamin Yang studies International Affairs at George Washington University's Elliott School, with interests in Indo-Pacific defense and security, U.S.–China relations, and economic security. He founded Indo-Pacific Record and directs its research agenda, editorial standards, and technical development. He writes source-linked analysis of regional military affairs, defense policy, and the strategic narratives conveyed through official accounts. He also designed IPR's automated research archive, using Python, SQLite, and GitHub Actions to preserve official publications, document collection gaps, and support transparent, reproducible editorial work. Beyond IPR, he leads the Strategic Materials Policy Tracker, which examines government interventions in critical-material supply chains, and has published analysis in The Diplomat on U.S.–China exchange. He is also an Associate Editor at The Globe, George Washington University's undergraduate international affairs research journal.

name: Dylan Tanzi
bio: Dylan Tanzi studies International Politics at Georgetown University's Walsh School of Foreign Service. As Lead Research Analyst at Indo-Pacific Record, he has helped establish the Vietnam Research Desk and expand the publication's Southeast Asian coverage. His work focuses on primary-source research, translation verification, and editorial review of regional security and foreign policy analysis, with particular interests in Southeast Asian affairs, international security, and historical memory.

name: Christin Sawyer
bio: Christin Sawyer studies International Affairs at George Washington University. As Communications Editor at Indo-Pacific Record, she supports the presentation and distribution of source-grounded research through visual explainers, editorial updates, and public-facing communications. Fluent in Korean and English, she brings language skills and a cross-cultural perspective to the publication's coverage of Indo-Pacific affairs.
